html:
Amir Khusrau was a poet, musician and scholar of the Delhi Sultanate, born in 1253 and active at court for some fifty years. He is one of the founders of the shared Hindu and Muslim culture of north India.

His father was a Turkish officer and his mother Indian. He served a string of sultans, from the Mamluks through Alauddin Khalji to the Tughlaqs, writing their praise and histories of their wars. Most of his work is in Persian, but he also wrote riddles and songs in Hindavi, the ancestor of Hindi and Urdu.

He was the devoted student of the Sufi master Nizamuddin Auliya of the Chishti order. He died a few months after his teacher in 1325 and is buried near him in Delhi.

Tradition credits him with founding qawwali and with shaping Hindustani music. Stories that he invented the sitar and tabla are probably later legend. He called himself proud to be Indian and praised India above Persia in his poems.
